name: Monterey Bay Kelp Forest
blurb: Giant kelp, urchins and the sea otters that keep the forest standing.

tip.title: Remove the sea otters
tip.text: Otters eat urchins, which graze kelp. Set Southern sea otter to -100% and watch urchins, then the kelp and everything that lives in it.

notes: Feeding links were checked against the sources listed where they state them. Where the sources are silent, links come from general ecological knowledge and are illustrative. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Kelp needs light reaching the canopy near the surface; dense canopy shades the water and seafloor below.

nodes.name: Cool nutrient-rich water
nodes.desc: Cold, nutrient-bearing water from the deep ocean feeds the algae and plankton of the bay.

nodes.name: Cool water temperature
nodes.desc: Giant kelp does best in cool water, mostly below about 21 C. Warm El Nino water has been known to kill it.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead kelp, plankton and animals, returning nutrients to the water.

nodes.name: Giant kelp
nodes.desc: Fast-growing brown alga anchored to rock that forms a floating canopy. Many animals depend on it for food or shelter.

nodes.name: Bull kelp
nodes.desc: A canopy kelp of central and northern California coasts, eaten by black abalone there along with drift algae.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae that feed filter feeders such as mussels. General ecological knowledge.

nodes.name: Purple sea urchin
nodes.desc: Grazes kelp, often eating drifting pieces. Without enough predators it can multiply and strip an area bare, leaving an urchin barren.

nodes.name: Black abalone
nodes.desc: A herbivorous snail that feeds mostly on drift algae and kelp. Critically endangered after overfishing and withering syndrome.

nodes.name: Kelp crab
nodes.desc: A crab of kelp holdfasts and canopy that grazes on kelp; kelp crabs are among the animals that eat kelp.

nodes.name: Amphipods and small crustaceans
nodes.desc: Small crustaceans that live among the kelp and feed on its tissue and drift. Food for small fish.

nodes.name: California mussel
nodes.desc: Filters plankton from the water on wave-washed rock. Sea otters feed on mussels and so open up space on the rock for other species.

nodes.name: Sunflower sea star
nodes.desc: A big predatory sea star that eats many urchins. Sea star wasting disease wiped it out from California waters from 2013, and urchins have been rising since.

nodes.name: Southern sea otter
nodes.desc: Eats urchins, abalone, crabs and mussels, which keeps urchin numbers down and lets kelp grow. Great white sharks are its main predator in California.

nodes.name: Rockfish
nodes.desc: Use the kelp understory for shelter and feeding, taking small invertebrates there.

nodes.name: Harbor seal
nodes.desc: Feeds on fish near the forest edges. Harbor seals are among the main prey of great white sharks in California.

nodes.name: California sea lion
nodes.desc: Hunts fish around kelp forest edges and is a main target of white sharks off California.

nodes.name: Great white shark
nodes.desc: Preys mainly on seals and sea lions off California. Bites sea otters often but usually does not eat them.

nodes.name: Orca
nodes.desc: The main mammalian predator of sea otters, and has killed great white sharks off California. Also eats seals and sea lions.

link_ideas.what: Orca predation on white sharks recorded at the Farallones, linking Monterey Bay shark and orca movements
